name: Pont Neuf
locality: 6th arrondissement of Paris; Quartier de la Monnaie; Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois
heritage: classified historical monument; part of UNESCO World Heritage Site
text: The Pont Neuf (French pronunciation: [pɔ̃ nœf], "New Bridge") is the oldest standing bridge across the river Seine in Paris, France. It stands by the western (downstream) point of the Île de la Cité, the island in the middle of the river that between 250 and 225 BC was the birthplace of Paris (then known as Lutetia). During the medieval period, the Île was the heart of the city.
